📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patch [Fri 13th Nov 2026, 5:45pm]: Well, unfortunately we have answer - Xbox engineer Eden Marie has confirmed over on BlueSky that the inclusion of Fable III in this image was an "error".

While the post itself is private, it reads as follows (and thanks to Pure Xbox user TheBillConiglio for alerting us to this):.

"Bill: Seeing an image of a library with Fable 3 having a disc to digital badge. Error, or......".

Original Story: Yesterday, Xbox starting rolling out three new console features for Xbox Insiders to try out: rotating home backgrounds, the ability to choose which side the Xbox guide pops open on, and new ways to organise disc to digital games.

They're all cool features that we're definitely keen to play around with, but what got our attention most was the image Xbox used to show off the latest disc to digital upgrade. Particularly, the games featured with the D2D licence icon plopped in the bottom-left corner of each game tile.

Industry observers note that did Xbox just tease the inclusion of Xbox 360 games in the D2D programme? Well, that would be true if the image depicting Fable III is to be taken at face value. At a glance, you'd probably see the image above and think, 'great, that's awesome', but the more you look at it, the weirder it gets.

Industry observers note that avowed famously released on Xbox without a physical disc. So, if the theory about Xbox 360 games joining the programme is on the money, does that mean we're getting a physical copy of Avowed too? And what about Age of Empires IV? That never received a physical release either. Then If we really want to go Enola Holmes on this image, Forza games aren't D2D compatible.

We're thinking someone at Xbox might've messed up with this image. Announcements of this magnitude shouldn't be buried in an Xbox Insider upgrade. Xbox should be shouting about it on the front page. So, why do an Xbox 360 game and two digital-only titles have D2D icons attached to them? I could think of a lazy reason.

Only time will tell, but consider us sceptical for now. We've chalked this one up to a blunder from Xbox, although it wouldn't surprise us if Xbox 360 games did eventually join the D2D programme. And hey, it's Xbox's birthday this Sunday. Maybe there's more to this than meets the eye.

Recent findings suggest that what do you make of this? Is it a mess up, or something really exciting? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that what is Formula 1 if not just very fast, mechanical horse racing? Surely I'm not the only one who has asked that question, especially considering the Japanese Grand Prix leg of the 2027 F1 World Championship has just revealed that Cygame's horse girl gacha Umamusume: Pretty Derby has become a founding partner.

Industry observers note that what does that mean in practice? Well, according to a press release, founding partners are "the highest tier supporters of the F1 Japanese Grand Prix," where they "bring additional value to the event while helping to shape the direction of its growth. Through marketing, promotional activities, and creating upcoming experiences for fans, Umamusume will continue contributing to the long term growth of the Japanese Grand Prix.".

Industry observers note that in layman's terms, that'll be a tidy sum of money invested into the Japanese Grand Prix, and in Umamusume's case it also means slapping its name on one of Suzuka Circuit's iconic corners—changing the name from the 130R corner to Umamusume 130R for around a year. Unsurprisingly, there'll also be a bit of Umamusume marketing and branding splashed across a banner or two, though Cygames claims that none of it will be on display during the actual Japanese Grand Prix itself.

(I'm also learning today that F1 circuit corners have names. Neat.).

Recent findings suggest that in case you're not familiar with Umamusume's whole schtick, it's an anime-slash-gacha-game all about anthropomorphised horse girls. Ones who are also based on real-life race horses, by the by. The gacha's global release brought tons of eyes onto the franchise last year, and its fans have done an awful lot of good—stuff like donating so much grass to the horse girl's real-life counterparts that it broke the donation website, or raising hundreds of thousands of dollars towards renovating stables.

It's a fun little collaboration between two vastly different sports, and I imagine there's definitely a good chunk of folks who sit in the Venn diagram of "F1 fan" and "horse girl fan". For those who do lie firmly in between those two fandoms, Cygames is also opening a special booth at Suzuka Circuit, as well as a mysterious "special live music performance" taking place on April 10. Considering Umamusume has plenty of original music (since it's also kind of an idol game… it's hard to explain, okay?) I wouldn't be surprised if we'll be hearing a ditty or two from the likes of Silence Suzuka and Special Week.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A latest Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major revision. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

According to recent reports, as everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

Recent findings suggest that the hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this patch. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

Industry observers note that in combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

According to recent reports, returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

In a recent development, version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, sega have revealed that over two million email addresses have leaked due to a cyberattack on Japanese email delivery provider Arara, whom the Like A Dragon and Sonic publishers use to distribute newsletters.
  • Sources indicate that according to Automaton, who've translated Sega's official press release about the cyberattack, 2,196,044 email addresses in total were affected.
  • The firm have listed some specific newsletter releases as having been affected, including two exhibition announcements for this year's Tokyo Game Show, the announcement of arcade rhythm game Chunithm Mate's launch, six newsletters about online character lottery service Sega Lucky Kuji Online, the launch of a rhythm game patch dubbed Ongeki Re:Fresh Act.2, and the launch of another arcade rhythm game update called Maimai DX MAGiCAL.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, sega have revealed that over two million email addresses have leaked due to a cyberattack on Japanese email delivery provider Arara, whom the Like A Dragon and Sonic publishers use to distribute newsletters. Sega and Arara are currently busy investigating what happened in the breach, which doesn't appear to have affected the Sega accounts you can use receive in-game rewards and access a calendar which reminds you when it's Kazuma Kiryu's birthday. The companies have urged those who signed up for the affected newsletters to be wary of potential phishing attempts.

Sources indicate that according to Automaton, who've translated Sega's official press release about the cyberattack, 2,196,044 email addresses in total were affected. 92,273 of that number were linked to the newsletter distribution.

The firm have listed some specific newsletter releases as having been affected, including two exhibition announcements for this year's Tokyo Game Show, the announcement of arcade rhythm game Chunithm Mate's launch, six newsletters about online character lottery service Sega Lucky Kuji Online, the launch of a rhythm game patch dubbed Ongeki Re:Fresh Act.2, and the launch of another arcade rhythm game update called Maimai DX MAGiCAL. Number one, that's a lot of rhythm games, and number two, Sega have advised those who opted in and received those newsletters to watch out for fishing emails from people posing as being tied to Sega or Arara.

It has been revealed that sega reportedly confirmed that - as far as the affected emails go - no names, dates of birth, genders, residential addresses, phone numbers, credit card information, and passwords are known to have been leaked. There had also been no reports of cases where the leaked information had been misused as of the time Sega made their announcement. The firm have naturally put distributing any further email newsletters through Arara on hold until their investigation's done and initiative to reach out to each affected person individually once the full details of the leak have been confirmed.

While data breaches and cyberattacks are nothing fresh, there have been a fair few recently, with both Street Fighter makers Capcom and Kingdom Come Deliverance 2 devs Warhorse suffering incidents of their own last month.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft is reportedly working on two fresh Assassin's Creed games, and one of them is set in ancient Rome.

That's according to YouTuber Xj0nathan, who indicates the Rome game is codenamed Mars. He claims two sources with access to Ubisoft's backend systems backed up the information, and that the setting will likely be linked to the upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series.

The second game, codenamed Pocket, is mentioned to be a mobile title set in Jerusalem. Xj0nathan claims it'll play a bit like Assassin’s Creed Valhalla’s Mastery Challenge, and look similar to the most recent Prince of Persia. The hero's mentor is apparently a character called Myriam.

Industry observers note that insider Gaming indicates it's heard the codenames too, but couldn't confirm them well enough to report them independently. It puts some of that down to the turbulence the franchise has gone through since former Assassin's Creed boss Marc-Alexis Côté left Ubisoft.

Last month, the outlet's sources also claimed Assassin's Creed Hexe, the next mainline game, had been delayed internally by another year, likely to 2028. Other reports claim we'll see it next year.

If Mars does move into full production, don't hold your breath - Insider Gaming doesn't expect us to hear anything about it until 2029 or 2030.

Assassin's Creed has visited Rome before, in 2010’s Brotherhood, but that was the Renaissance version of the city.

The leak comes less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are right now no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, personally, I still haven't wrapped my head around BioWare's closure. The legendary home of Mass Effect, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and Dragon Age was a standard-bearer in modern RPG design for so long; it seemed like it could weather any storm. Alas, the industry right now is difficult, but even former leadership is struggling to comprehend this turn of events.

In a recent development, on The Critical Path podcast, Casey Hudson, former BioWare general manager and creator of the original Mass Effect, explained where his head's at as the company closes. "Part of the reason I came back and wanted to be GM of the studio, and was interested in that, was because I've just got so many friends there and I love the studio," he indicates.

And I wanted to do whatever I could in the years I was there to try and set it up for some kind of longevity," he explains. Hudson left BioWare twice: first exiting in 2014 and winding up at Microsoft for a spell, then returning to upper management in 2017 before leaving again in 2020.

According to recent reports, "There are things that you think are just going to last forever," he adds. "But I think that even though we all worried that the day would come when it would get shut down, it's still a different feeling to realize that it is actually closed.".

I suspect the notion of an unceremonious end lingered in the air quite a few times, especially over the last ten years or so. You had the rocky reception to Mass Effect: Andromeda, and the years it took to make Dragon Age: The Veilguard, only for the game to get a muted response. These are the kinds of things that can make any studio unsustainable.

But it always seemed like BioWare had another banger in it, and what we've heard about Mass Effect 5 indicated the team had the right ideas. Hudson mentions that he's among the chorus wondering if we'll ever get some version of that game. EA could sell the franchise to someone else, but it may hoard the dormant IP, too.

According to recent reports, "It's very difficult," he comments. "Especially for folks that I know that are on that team. I think everyone's just hoping there's some way forward, both individually for folks in their careers, but also for the great games that BioWare made.".

This next major patch arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Recent findings suggest that most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

It has been revealed that among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

It has been revealed that when she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other newly introduced Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very crucial action in the core story, this chapter also brings upcoming themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting Firefight as a free update, though I'm not sure it'll do much to change the remake's fortunes

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (588 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xbox has declared the first upgrade for Halo: Campaign Evolved since August, one which will add Firefight to the remake's overhaul of the original game's story.
  • Recent findings suggest that firefight is Halo's cooperative PvE mode which debuted in Halo 3: ODST.
  • Sources indicate that in its announcement, Xbox was extremely light on details regarding the addition of Firefight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xbox has declared the first upgrade for Halo: Campaign Evolved since August, one which will add Firefight to the remake's overhaul of the original game's story.

Recent findings suggest that firefight is Halo's cooperative PvE mode which debuted in Halo 3: ODST. It's a round-based defence affair where players must survive as long as possible against increasingly dangerous waves of enemies. Following ODST, the mode appeared in every subsequent Halo game with the exception of Halo 4, which featured a mode called Spartan Ops instead.

Sources indicate that in its announcement, Xbox was extremely light on details regarding the addition of Firefight. But the manufacturer remarked it'll share "additional details" about the Firefight enhancement during Halo Fest, which takes place over the weekend commencing December 12.

I'm pleased to see Campaign Evolved getting some more features, but the announcement also increases my sense that Xbox really doesn't know what to do with Halo at present. Campaign Evolved itself felt like a collective shrug from Halo Studios, a glossy but unambitious overhaul of the original game, with three upcoming levels that nobody liked and shorn of the multiplayer that the PC version so enjoyable in the early 2000s.

Recent findings suggest that morgan Park felt similarly in his Halo: Campaign Evolved Review. "It was cool to see another interpretation of a game special to me, but the glitzy coat of paint primarily highlights how right Bungie got it in 2001, and how its modern stewards are nudging Halo in an unremarkable direction," he wrote back in July.

A Firefight mode, coming nearly six months after launch with almost complete radio silence since August, smacks more of "We need something for Halo Fest" than the start of a bright upcoming future for the remake. Not that I expected it to magically rejuvenate Halo. But that lack of expectation, of anticipation, is in itself part of the problem.

Recent findings suggest that I could be wrong, of course. As part of Xbox's "reset"—which has included laying off thousands of staff and saying sayonara to several studios—Xbox also handed control of Halo over to Activision. So perhaps bringing back Firefight is the first step in Activision's plan—whatever that is. Some have suggested that Xbox wants Halo to be a more Call of Duty-like experience, which would certainly make sense from Xbox's perspective. Whether Halo can actually be that is, of course, another matter entirely.

"But sire!" I would have told him, if I'd been one of the aforesaid lickspittles. "Why not lay down spike strips and park a couple of flamethrowers in the shallows?" I would have said this because I have just been playing Swarmbreaker, a tower defence game that aims to prove there is no fluid body so awe-inspiring that it cannot be machine-gunned into submission.

Industry observers note that in Swarmbreaker - which launches on Steam tomorrow, and still has a demo as of writing – you have to defend your rocketship against waves of insect aggressors, who spawn at the map's far corners. Between waves, you spend earnings from kills on turrets, barricades, troops, and upgrades for all the foregoing. Sounds like bog-standard attrition management, perhaps, but what lifts Swarmbreaker is the "swarm" part. The rapacious scuttlers come in several distinct varieties, but they also "cluster, collide and flow like a fluid".

The results are hypnotic: coloured particles burst from each burrow and course through the map's contours, pushing movable terrain elements and eroding your structures like acid. You can practically hear the oil derricks fizz as they are engulfed and chewed to a lumpy puddle of iridescent digestive enzymes. Speaking of which, the more oil derricks you save during each wave, the more cash you'll have to spend before the next, but committing to their protection obviously risks leaving your ship exposed. Your fallback option is an inexhaustible mouse-click-fired artillery cannon, but this won't save you if the bulk of the swarm makes it all the way to your doorstep.

Sources indicate that I'm still not convinced this isn't a run-of-the-mill tower defender, beneath it all, but it's worth giving the demo a shot just to enjoy the swirling tidal dynamics of homocidal buglife. What would King Canute have made of it all? I think he would have stuck his throne right by the biggest burrow, surrounded by gravity traps and howitzers. "Back in your hole, hungry liquids!" he'd have bellowed, firing dual AK47s simultaneously. "The only god I recognise is efficient chokepoint management! Death to sense-of-flow! Death to trickle-down politics!".

Sources indicate that "SIRE," I'd have told him sternly. "You are getting your metaphors confused. And also that is a total waste of howitzers - those things are best placed on hills." Read more on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Double Fine released Kiln as an Xbox first-party title last year, it's fair to say a lot of the Xbox fanbase was baffled by it. As much as it was a good game (we gave it a 7/10 in our Pure Xbox review), it also shipped with just a singular, online-only mode that was bound to get old pretty promptly.

Double Fine ended up being let go by Xbox, turning Kiln from an Xbox first-party game into an independent game, and it received a brand-latest update back in September, adding a new creative game mode along with various other features.

But today, to mark the planned end of development, it's received its biggest enhancement of all time - adding in three newly introduced game modes, an increased level cap, a Photo Booth and loads more besides.

Here's a look at just the highlights of this latest update:.

In terms of the three modes, Fire Fighter is a 4v4 mode where "both teams are in a mad dash to catch a flaming Chimenea", Stoked is also a 4v4 mode that's "all about igniting the Pyres with your team’s flame", and Local Mini Quench is a smaller version of the original Quench mode that can be played with up to three other people offline.

Offline mode is actually classed as a separate upcoming feature as well:.

Recent findings suggest that "As part of being able to play locally, we’ve added an offline mode. This allows you to play and practice without needing to worry about your Ping or people. This, alongside the player hosted matches and account change, helps future-proof Kiln so that you can play it for years to come!".

It has been revealed that pretty cool, right? On top of that, Kiln has received a brand-latest identity this week in the form of "Kiln: Reshaped", with the name change serving as a way to "let you know how much is in this update!".

Unfortunately, it does seem like Kiln's flame has already been doused for the majority of players at this point, but it's great to see Double Fine putting in the work to not only preserve it for the future, but hopefully light the spark once again for people who have fallen away from it in recent months.

Don't forget it's on Xbox Game Pass as well, or available on the Xbox Store for just £6.99 / $7.99.

What are your final thoughts on Kiln? Will you be checking out this update? Tell us down below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has delayed its Pulse Elevate wireless speakers indefinitely, less than a week before they were due to launch.

The news came in a 6th November revision to Sony’s original announcement on the PlayStation Blog, first spotted by IGN. Quality testing has turned up a "production problem", Sony said, and there's no new release date yet.

Sources indicate that "As part of our ongoing quality testing of Pulse Elevate speakers, we have identified a production matter with the product and have made the decision to delay the launch," the statement reads. "The additional time will allow us to ensure the product will deliver the experience we intended for our players. We apologise for the delay and appreciate your patience and understanding. We look forward to bringing Pulse Elevate to players soon.".

In a recent development, the speakers were set to go on sale worldwide on 12th November, and pre-orders opened in September. It's unclear what, exactly, happens to those orders, but we'll update as and when we find out more.

In a recent development, sony revealed Pulse Elevate in September 2025 as its first wireless speakers for desktop gaming. They sit alongside the Pulse Elite headset and Pulse Explore earbuds, and cost £199.99 ($219.99).

They connect to PS5, PC, Mac, and PlayStation Portal via PlayStation Link, and can pair with a phone over Bluetooth at the same time. There's also a microphone in the right speaker with what Sony calls "AI-enhanced noise rejection".

Midnight Black was due to be available everywhere, while the White version was limited to a handful of countries, including the UK.

Alongside the Pulse Elevate speakers, Sony revealed a range of hardware in September 2025, including a 27-inch gaming monitor that's coming only to the US and Japan.

It has been revealed that the Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS) has announced that Shigeru Miyamoto, the creator of iconic Nintendo franchises like Super Mario and The Legend of Zelda, will receive the inaugural Legend Award at the upcoming 30th Annual D.I.C.E. Awards ceremony on Thursday, 18th February 2027.

The award, which will only be presented once per decade, 'recognises an industry icon whose enduring vision continues to redefine interactive entertainment'. It's designed to honour creators whose achievements have already earning lasting universal acclaim, while celebrating their 'immeasurable impact and influence'.

Meggan Scavio, President of the AIAS, said the following:.

It has been revealed that “Shigeru Miyamoto is widely recognized as one of the most respected and impactful figures in the games industry and beyond. We believe he perfectly embodies our inaugural Legend Award through his impact and reach, and we are so humbled and excited to have Mr. Miyamoto accept this award at the 30th anniversary of the D.I.C.E. Awards.".

Though his current focus is on the production of movies and theme parks, Miyamoto-san is arguably the most recognisable figure in Nintendo's history, and it's difficult to imagine whether the manufacturer would even exist today without his creations.

He most recently appeared during a Pikmin Day Direct presentation, during which he revealed a newly introduced demo for Pikmin 4 on Switch 2 along with some Pikmin Bloom updates and the commencement of monthly Hello! Pikmin movies on the Nintendo Today app.

Breaking: Explaining Super Smash Bros was a nightmare, notes Masahiro Sakurai, because it wasn't Street Fighter

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (479 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you'd think something like Super Smash Bros.
  • According to recent reports, the longtime figurehead of the Smash Bros series recalled the conversations for Denfamicogamer.
  • It has been revealed that he notes that if it had shipped with mechanics similar to Street Fighter or Tekken, it would've been seen as a "novelty" and not lasted the way it has.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you'd think something like Super Smash Bros. would be easy to sell. It's Pikachu, Link and Mario fighting each other – what's not to love? Well, creator Masahiro Sakurai has revealed it was a difficult pitch because of his platformer-inspired vision of the gameplay.

According to recent reports, the longtime figurehead of the Smash Bros series recalled the conversations for Denfamicogamer. "Think about if Smash Bros. had normal fighting game rules," he states, translated by Nintendo Everything. "In a one-on-one battle, you'd have guard, attack, and special attacks, and once your energy is depleted, you're KOed and the match is over. I don’t think the original Smash Bros. would have been released like that.".

It has been revealed that he notes that if it had shipped with mechanics similar to Street Fighter or Tekken, it would've been seen as a "novelty" and not lasted the way it has. "I made the game confidently believing that the ingenuity of Smash Bros. and gameplay hooks of elements such as damage accumulation and positioning would be fun," he recalls.

"At the time though, it was criticized by people who couldn’t get into the differences it had from Street Fighter 2 and Virtua Fighter," he says.

Recent findings suggest that I can believe it. The original Super Smash Bros. stood out like a sore thumb in the fighting game landscape. The series still does, to an extent, but between its own legacy and a number of clones and pretenders, it's not as singular within the industry.

Sakurai then doubles down on the trickiness of selling the core ideas internally. "But it’s actually very difficult to 'intentionally add ingenuity,'" he adds. "When there are no previous examples, it’s very difficult to explain to staff, and it’s also very key - and difficult - to think about how to aim for and proceed towards what we want.".

According to recent reports, at least we know he was successful. Craving your own path can be hard, especially when it involves pitting beloved characters against each other in a novel way.

Super Smash Bros creator Masahiro Sakurai says "there's no way" he can talk about what he's working on, so fans are doing it for him.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Star Wars Zero Organization developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.

Several developers revealed on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't mentioned how many people are affected.

Sources indicate that among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.

Sources indicate that "While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you.".

Recent findings suggest that bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Tech giant launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.

It has been revealed that the game did well regardless, and is thought to have sold more than a million copies within a month. Then, in a message shared on Bluesky on 7th October, CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process of returning more of our team back to work". Asking staff to step away so close to launch was "an incredibly difficult decision", he said, "but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible".

According to recent reports, it's thought more than half the studio returned, though not everyone went back on full pay. It's not clear whether any of those who returned were among the people laid off this week.

In Eurogamer's Star Wars Zero Manufacturer review, we awarded the game four out of five stars, saying, "an already winning genre is matched with the perfect setting in this earnest, heartfelt, smart and slightly ramshackle turn-based tactics gem".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed.
  • All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.
  • In a recent development, it has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert released on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crimson Desert, the open-world action RPG off-shoot from Korean MMO Black Desert Online, has officially launched, nearly six years after it was initially revealed. The game has been building up a lot of momentum over the years, which recently coalesced to turn it into one of 2026’s most anticipated titles.

All of it has been leading up to this moment, and the game appears to have landed smoothly, though not without controversy, as has seemingly become part of its MO.

In a recent development, it has not been 24 hours since Crimson Desert released on PC and consoles, and it’s already become a big hit. On Steam, one of two stores where the game can be purchased (the other being the Epic Games Store), the game shot to the top of the charts.

The action RPG continued to accumulate more and more players on Steam, peaking at a very respectable 239,045 concurrent players (via SteamDB). Though its success was very much expected, we perhaps didn’t predict its peak would be that high.

Industry observers note that indeed, Crimson Desert has been in Steam’s top 100 global sellers list for six weeks, jumping up six spots to become the number one seller this week just before it released. As we get closer to the weekend, the numbers could climb even higher.

It has been revealed that this peak concurrent puts Crimson Desert in the same league as several of the other major releases of the first quarter of 2026. The top spot continues to belong to Slay the Spire 2, which peaked at a staggering 574,638 concurrent players. It happened just days after the juggernaut Resident Evil Requiem achieved its own 344,214 peak concurrent, which was the year’s highest up until Slay the Spire 2’s release. All three are well ahead of Nioh 3’s 88,045 peak concurrent, and Marathon’s nearly identical peak of 88,337.

Recent findings suggest that crimson Desert has seen something of a mixed reception by critics. James gave it three stars in our review, saying it “lacks the connective sinew to be truly functional,” which is a common criticism shared by other outlets. Many also lamented the sheer number of systems fighting for player attention, its poorly explained mechanics, and counterintuitive controls.

On Steam, at least, players have similarly been divided, with the current Steam user rating sitting at Mixed, based on 8,728 reviews. Unsurprisingly, most of the negative reactions fall on the clunky controls and the game’s tendency to, as one Steam user put it, “so miserably tries to be everything at once, and fails to be anything at all.”.

If you’re just getting started in Crimson Desert yourself, or strategy to do so soon, we recommend reading these crucial tips to help orient yourself in the game’s vast world. You should also plan your initial skill unlocks by prioritising these skills to spend your Abyss Artifacts first.

#17040. Dishonored 2 director Harvey Smith wants to honour sacred imsim texts while finding newly introduced ways to surprise fans: 'That's the two wolves inside me'

Dishonored 2 director Harvey Smith wants to honour sacred imsim texts while finding newly introduced ways to surprise fans: 'That's the two wolves inside me'

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1848 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harvey Smith remembers the 10 months he spent as quality assurance lead on System Shock as a "brush with greatness".
  • "I had loved Ultima Underworld, and then I got to work with the very people that were rolling off of Underworld onto this newly introduced cyberpunk game," he says.
  • Sources indicate that afterwards, when Smith joined System Shock producer Warren Spector at Ion Storm Austin, "we just applied that same hunger to Deus Ex," he claims.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Harvey Smith remembers the 10 months he spent as quality assurance lead on System Shock as a "brush with greatness".

"I had loved Ultima Underworld, and then I got to work with the very people that were rolling off of Underworld onto this newly introduced cyberpunk game," he says. "Looking Glass fought like cats and dogs, but man, they were passionate about what they were doing. And this was a mission for them.".

Sources indicate that afterwards, when Smith joined System Shock producer Warren Spector at Ion Storm Austin, "we just applied that same hunger to Deus Ex," he claims. "And then when I got together with Raphaël Colantonio, we were like, 'Why just live a normal life? Why fucking punch in and sit at a desk and run some numbers? We're just dying to do this, right?' And so we made Dishonored.".

It's a simplified take on the story—one that skips the wilderness years spent fighting for funding before Arkane partnered with Bethesda. But the stubborn and single-minded outlook Smith describes is crucial to explaining his career in immersive sims. If he had been more sensible—less determined to funnel his days into spiritually satisfying work in the genre that first lit his creative fire—Arkane would never have made Dishonored at all.

"When Arkane was independent, very often people would come in and they would try to get us to work on some game that was not in our wheelhouse," he indicates. "People would say, 'You're going to go under by turning your nose up at doing this DLC for this third-person action shooter, this is money.' And we'd be like, 'Yeah, but we don't like those. We don't know how to do them well, and we think that game is dumb. So we're generally going to say no, and gamble the firm on doing what we are known for.'".

Recent findings suggest that arkane very nearly did go under, pursuing its dogged goal of making immersive sims. But eventually, that doggedness was recognised by its peers in the games industry.

There are many ways to fail, many ways to succeed. But specialising in what you love is not a bad path.

"There was a moment we were pretty desperate, and a bunch of people working on BioShock 2 noted, 'God, we're in a tight spot. We need somebody to take on a bunch of levels. You know who's out there? Arkane.' So we took Christophe Carrier, our level design director, who is really the wellspring from which a lot of that thinking at Arkane came from. We took him and a team, and we put them on BioShock 2. And that only happened because people associated us with that kind of game.".

Keep up to date with the most vital stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Sources indicate that by saying "no" enough times, Arkane defined itself clearly in the eyes of its fellows—as a team of consummate worldbuilders and determined architects of intricate first-person levels that rewarded deep exploration. In time, players came to recognise the studio for the same thing, and loved Arkane for it. "In a sense the purity was more valuable than the jack-of-all-trades," Smith states. "There are many ways to fail, many ways to succeed. But specialising in what you love is not a bad path.".

Sources indicate that things only really went wrong a decade after Dishonored, with Redfall—the FPS that struggled to incorporate imsim values into co-op looter-shooting. "That was a game that did not come together," Smith says. "And we never should have been working on a games-as-a-service game, to be honest.".

With its sleepy Massachusetts backdrop, leftfield movement abilities and a grounded theme of community resistance in the face of corporate greed, Redfall had some memorable and redeeming features. But it was a disappointment, and became a lightning rod for criticism of Xbox, who by that time was Arkane's owner.

"There were many things that seemed to converge all at once when Redfall was releasing," indicates Ben Horne, the production director of Redfall who co-founded Black Pony Immersive along with Smith. "I believe it was the first $70 price point game that Xbox had put out at the time. It was, I think, subject to some of the console wars.".

To make matters worse, Arkane had developed a performance mode for Redfall on consoles, but held it back after noticing dips in its framerate. "That turned into a huge thing where people came and said, 'Oh, how come this isn't 60 fps at launch?,'" Horne says. "And so there were all of those things that were happening that we were trying to manage, but I think the bigger concern there is that we were working on something that was just outside of our expertise. Getting back to what we do best was the number one priority. For Harvey and myself, for the folks at Arkane and now at Black Pony, this is what our focus is.".

Sometimes it blows up in our face, and sometimes it results in Deus Ex or Dishonored.

It has been revealed that smith and Horne co-founded Black Pony Immersive in the wake of Arkane Austin's closure, with the explicit goal of making immersive sims. Before Redfall, Horne had worked for years on annual NBA games in California. "You know occasionally you meet somebody who's on fire, they're very talented, and you can tell that they're hungry for something that is out there?," Smith says. "I've been in games 33 years now, and I would never want to weaponise this, but I can always tell when somebody needs something more substantial or more spiritual in their lives professionally. And that is, honestly, what we chase all the time. Sometimes it blows up in our face, and sometimes it results in Deus Ex or Dishonored.".

Horne, for his part, still remembers his first day at Arkane. "Production director Susan Kath came up to me and was just like, 'Hey, why don't you play this build? We're about to release this DLC'. I think I left the office at midnight. I could not pull away from it.".

Sources indicate that the creative director of that DLC, Prey: Mooncrash, was Ricardo Bare, who also works at Black Pony today. "Ricardo is a deep thinker about the cosmos and what sentience, awareness and consciousness are," Smith says. "If you play Prey, you get to hear people asking questions about why some creatures are capable of empathy and some are not. Ricardo likes to think about those things, so while he's also a game designer and a writer and thinks about literary themes, he comes in thinking about that metaphysical layer as well.".

It has been revealed that the games Smith directs, meanwhile, have consistently explored systems of power and exploitation. "Dishonored is underpinned by that theme," he states. "The Outsider overtly and indirectly talks about themes related to the abuse of power. And you know, Deus Ex was a political awakening for me. I didn't know that much about politics, embarrassingly enough, when I was in my 20s, and I started working with Warren Spector.".

Recent findings suggest that smith and Spector collaborated for nine years across two Deus Ex games. "Warren was well-versed in the way politics and power work across the world," Smith says. "The personal is the political because someone has power over your life.".

Somewhere in the mix of these themes, perhaps, is the key to understanding the perspective of Black Pony's unannounced debut game. And mechanically speaking, we already know exactly what to expect. "First-person games that are a hybrid of shooter, stealth and RPG, where the player can be creative and explore," Smith says. "It's very player-paced, it's singleplayer, it's narrative-driven. There's a lot of atmospherics. That's what we burn to do.".

In a recent development, during the years that Smith and Colantonio co-directed Dishonored, they shared an office and spent lots of time travelling together—discussing the precepts of the genre they'd devoted their professional lives to. "We realised that when it comes to immersive sims, some people are very dogmatic," Smith says. "They want to carry forward the sacred writings. You can't deviate from that, or you're a heretic. And other people are like, 'Yeah, sure, this is a cool base, but where can we go with it? What can we do that's new?' And that is always the challenge. That's the two wolves inside me. On one hand, I want to pay off those expectations. On the other hand, I want to exceed them.".

Smith is a substantial believer in systems that flow from a game's setting. In his experience, even familiar gameplay ideas can be revitalised by fresh fiction. One example is Dishonored's possession power, which began as Arkane's riff on disguises in Hitman.

"I need to put on the disguise so the guard won't kill me and I can walk past the other guards," Smith says. "But then we were like, 'Well, if I'm in his body, then I can walk through the Wall of Light because it's attuned to the guards. Or if I possess a rat, I can get into the rat tunnels and come into the building. And if I walk past the guard, the guard literally tries to stomp me because I'm a rat.'".

Let's hope Black Pony's not the one trick pony, right?

Suddenly, level designers were creating routes that allowed players to possess a fish in a fountain, follow the pipes up the u-bend, and emerge in the toilet of an assassination target. "We got a lot of love for that," Smith says. "But it was magical to us too.".

According to recent reports, he hopes the same approach will see Black Pony Immersive join Arkane, Ion Storm and Looking Glass in the lineage of great immersive sim studios. "Even if we're doing the same type of game we've done for a long time, we can find a way to take a thing we've done before and recontextualise it because of the newly introduced subject matter," he notes. "Let's hope Black Pony's not the one trick pony, right?".

#17039. Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

📅 10 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (1978 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1978 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that poema is my pride and joy.
  • Recent findings suggest that for all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface.
  • Recent findings suggest that there may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself.

Recent findings suggest that for all its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel.

Recent findings suggest that there may be better author comparisons, but I learned everything I know about showjumping from Cooper's Riders – much as I learned everything about independent television franchise bids in the '80s from its sequel Rivals – a book which is as much about the nitty gritty of horsetraining and competing as it is about toffs jumping into bed with one another. In my mind the two are tightly connected - showjumping and Jilly Cooper, not horses and toff bonking. In Horses of Hoofprint Bay, the only real story you get is the fact you've scrimped and saved to buy your first horse and your uncle has lent you the use of his field while you start your business. I was hoping there would at least be a similar setup to Regency Solitaire, where your motivation for touring the country's tearooms is motivated by paying off your brother's gambling debts. Yet, despite this disappointing start, I soon found its business simulation mechanics provide great storytelling material.

Horses of Hoofprint Bay has many of the trappings of a cosy game. At the start of each day, you'll prepare the stables, dragging a rake around the yard to sling away the manure, clicking buckets of water to refill the trough, and making sure there's enough hay for all the horses. But this isn't just for the larks, if you skip these tasks there are serious knock on effects for yours horses. Forget to brush down your horses' coats or pick out the stones in their shoes, and they're liable to develop saddle sores and other injuries when you ride them. Leave an abrasion untreated and it can develop into an infection. Even something like taking a dirty horse to a contest can cost you. I forgot to brush Poema before entering her into her first contest and despite taking first place, her embarrassingly unkempt coat lost my stable prestige. It was a cruel end to what should have been a great celebration.

Recent findings suggest that so long as your horses are well rested, you can train them each day. You may want to take them through some confidence building lunges, where they need to walk, trot, and canter on demand, or a more physically demanding Cavaletti or showjumping course. These latter too are much more tiring, but they build a horse's strength and endurance. The higher its endurance the more energy it can expend on training sessions each day, and the higher its strength the more jumps it can do in succession before slowing to a walk for a breather - essential when you're competing in a timed competition. Overdo the exercise, however, and you'll exhaust a horse, severely reducing its energy for the next day.

It has been revealed that now, unlike Poema, my freshly bought stallion Kolizey has the potential to compete in showjumping competitions. He'll never go all the way to the substantial national contests, but he can take a ribbon in the district and regional contests. Or he will when he's up to standard; he's arrived from the breeder in a sorry state: brambles in his mane, mud on his flanks, stones in his shoes, and his strength and endurance are far too low to make it through an entire course of obstacles.

The biggest problem, however, is Kolizey's confidence: it's shot. I don't know what was happening in the stalls at the breeder's, but he arrived at my stables backing up at the first sign of a jump. Before I can hope to earn him his first ribbon, I have to build up our relationship. If we exercise together enough in the yard, his confidence will grow and he will follow my direction without question.

Recent findings suggest that it may be getting ahead of myself, but I also have prepares for Kolizey and Poema to produce a foal. Done right, the two should raise a horse that's able to exceed its parents' potential, becoming stronger and more endurant than both of them. A stronger horse means a ticket to the bigger contests and the bigger prize pots. Not that I can start breeding the two just yet. I want both horses to be at peak physical fitness. Poema's already there, while Kolizey can't even manage a jump without shying away.

In a recent development, while getting Koliszey contest ready, I still need to be bringing in cash. That means using Poema as a training horse for students' riding lessons. The better I am at the minigame where I use the Q, E, W, A, S, and D keys to tell them to sit forward or back, hold the reins higher or lower, or to level out their legs, the more they tip me. I have to be careful, because when Poema is working with students, she's not being stretched, and her strength and endurance can wither which means she struggles to maintain her winning streak in the contests.

Sources indicate that another reason to hold off on getting Poema pregnant is that during the second half of her pregnancy, she can't be ridden, which means no contests and no lessons for students. Currently, those are my two main sources of income besides what I'm paid in rent to board a couple of nearby farmers' horses. I don't want her out of the rota when Kolizey isn't yet ready to step into her place.

And, well, while I'm on the subject of plans, reader, I must tell you, the future lies in semen. If I can build the facilities, earn the cash, and raise Kolizey's profile, I can make a good buck on his virile stallion cream. With the money I bring in from a prizewinning semen I can expand into the far field, creating space to take on more horses, upgrade my home from the caravan I'm living in currently, maybe even build a proper training school. I'm not going to afford all that by giving riding lessons to the local children or boarders' rent. No, the massive money comes from competition wins and valuable horse sauce.

While Poema continues entering contests and carrying students, I start pushing Kolizey harder. Multiple training sessions every day. I begin with Cavaletti, which is a kind of obedience competition. Your horse has to be travelling at the correct speed when it passes marker flags – walking, trotting, or cantering – and make some small jumps over cross bars. It should be straightforward, but because Kolizey's confidence is so low, he keeps refusing my orders and trying to change speed. He warns me before he's about to speed up or slow down, and if I counter it in time he will obey me and even receive a little confidence boost, but often he does it just before a jump, messing up my timing and he hits the bars. Each time he fails a jump it knocks his confidence, risking me taking me even further from where I need him to be.

Recent findings suggest that I try the easier lunges sessions. And they raise his confidence a little but they're doing little for his physical health. It's all taking too long and Poema's getting older every day. In a fit of frustration, and in mark that I may not be able to cut it as an animal trainer, I skip from the Cavaletti training straight into a showjumping qualifier. The time limits on these are much stricter, so you have to clear the course at a gallop. This is also where a horse's strength really comes into play. The faster you're going, the more strength it requires to jump an obstacle. Horses only recover strength when moving at a walk, so you don't want to tire a horse out by going at a gallop through the whole course, else they won't have the strength to make all the jumps and they'll be forced to withdraw from the event. But nor do you want to go too slowly and fall foul of the time limit.

It has been revealed that I realise my mistake as soon as the course begins: I try to stir Kolizey into a walk he refuses. Thankfully the timer only starts when he crosses the line, but it's an inauspicious start. I tap forward again and he begins to walk. I tap again and Kolizey moves up to a trot, then to a canter, before picking up to a gallop. I think he's going too fast as we approach the first jump, but Kolizey clears it. Then another jump and another. With a nervous eye on the depleting strength bar, I tap him down to a canter for the next jump. We're halfway through the course, I briefly slow to a walk to recover some strength then take the next three jumps at a canter. We're so close to the end now but a big yellow exclamation mark appears next to the strength bar. Kolizey is on the edge of exhaustion but he refuses to slow down and increases to a gallop for the last two jumps.

He completes the course with a perfect clear. Not a single obstacle clipped and we end with ten seconds left on the timer. Not only has Kolizey earned his showjumping license, his success swells his confidence. He's a natural athlete.

In a recent development, the next day, with my horses rested, I take Kolizey and Poema to town to compete in the showjumping and Caprilli events respectively. They both bring home first place, raising the prestige of my stables, earning me a tidy little packet, and convincing me it's time my prized horses started a family. I'm perhaps too eager, when I try to send them to the breeding station, I'm told they're both 'Done for the day'. I suppose I should give my contest winners a bit of a break. They've earned it. I groom them and send them both to bed with an apple as a treat.

According to recent reports, except, maybe they weren't too tired: the next morning, I'm met with a message telling me Poema is pregnant. My stable's become the Olympic Village, with my rosette-winning horses working out the highs and stresses of competition in the only way they know how. Good on them. I needn't have even made the breeding station.

Industry observers note that then, with horror, I remember the horses I'm boarding for the neighbours. They're both stallions themselves. Neither of them are at competition level, their strength and endurance is lower even than Poema's when she arrived at the stable. If either of them are the father, Poema is about to be out of action for a whole season and at the other end of it I'll have a foal that can't even compete in the beginner events. fetch the equestrian version of Hercule Poirot, I need to find out who impregnated my horse!

It may not be a plot worthy of Cooper, but it will do for me.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert has been out for a few days now, and as positive as its been received by many players, the game suffers from several fundamental issues that anyone who’s played it has called out.

Perhaps the loudest one of those has been how the game controls, which is a problem that stems from the complexity of controls themselves, as well as the underlying animations behind many of the actions the player character performs.

In the first case, at least, something is being done.

Developer Pearl Abyss rolled out patch 1.00.03 for Crimson Desert on Monday. The patch is available now on Steam and PlayStation, with Xbox and the Epic Games Store following “at a later time.”.

Today’s enhancement follows a letter to players the developer issued on Saturday. The letter generally acknowledged player feedback, but specifically pointed to complaints about the game’s clunky controls as something of a focus for the team.

The action RPG has actually broken its launch peak concurrent player numbers over the weekend, though only by a few thousands more. Its Steam user review rating has also improved over the same period.

Recent findings suggest that this latest update only includes an initial set of fixes, but Pearl Abyss vowed to keep working on addressing all other points of feedback. A highlight in 1.00.03 is the addition of a Storage at Howling Hill Camp, which can be used to store inventory items.

Recent findings suggest that the most vital changes, of course, affect how the game controls on keyboard and mouse. Pearl Abyss included several fixes and altered some of the default presets to make the experience less painful when playing the game with a keyboard and mouse.

There are sadly no changes to controllers, but it is something that the developer said we can expect to see in future patches. More improvements for keyboard and mouse setups are in the works, too.

Beyond the control changes, patch 1.00.03 also includes a set of gameplay tweaks, especially when it comes to enemy health and difficulty. It also makes fast travelling more convenient, and brings a few fixes to NPC dialogue. You can read the full change log on Steam.

If you’re deep in Crimson Desert already, we definitely recommend giving our guides a look. We recently added fresh pages to help you figure out where to socket your Abyss Gear, how to find Contribution Points - and where to spend them, as well as more generally helpful information like how to expand your inventory, and how to reveal the map.

GTA 6 studio head: "I'd never want to rebuild a city, I think that would be a lot less satisfying"

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GTA 6 co-studio head and long-time Rockstar art director Aaron Garbutt said he would "never want to rebuild a city" street-by-street, as it would be less satisfying for developer and player alike.
  • Speaking in Edge magazine back after the launch of GTA 5, Garbutt said that Rockstar's modern-day series "always use[d] the same process" when creating its open-worlds" "working with real cities, starting on a macro level to define the districts we want to use, and working down.".
  • "The only variation," he explained, "is how many real landmarks we decide to use once we get to the individual building level.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 co-studio head and long-time Rockstar art director Aaron Garbutt said he would "never want to rebuild a city" street-by-street, as it would be less satisfying for developer and player alike.

Speaking in Edge magazine back after the launch of GTA 5, Garbutt said that Rockstar's modern-day series "always use[d] the same process" when creating its open-worlds" "working with real cities, starting on a macro level to define the districts we want to use, and working down.".

"The only variation," he explained, "is how many real landmarks we decide to use once we get to the individual building level. I always feel we build our own world. We're still a long way from being dictated by reality." Instead, the real-life version of the city is "a starting point," in which Rockstar is prepared to move entire neighbourhoods around in search of its perfect game world.

Recent findings suggest that "I'd never want to rebuild a city," Garbutt explained. "I think that would be a lot less satisfying, both for us to build and for the player to play. In a lot of ways, it would be less convincing, too.".

The logic behind that philosophy is that most players won't actually know what the real city is like. "Only a relatively small subset of players ever get to know the real LA or Latest York," he noted, referring to Rockstar's Los Santos and Liberty City, the developers' interpretations of those real-life locations. Most people "experience [them] through film and TV, or just through short visits, and that's a highly edited representation.".

Sources indicate that and that was Rockstar's approach too: "We take the feel of a city, the one we get through visiting and through experiencing it our whole lives through media, and build that. We compress, we edit, we emphasize certain things and we end up with something that in some ways, I think, feels more like the popular perception of the place than the actual city.".

According to recent reports, GTA 5's Los Santos was arguably Rockstar's clearest attempt at that philosophy. GTA 4's Liberty City did a decent job of capturing New York, with its version of New Jersey relegated to the later stages of the game. San Andreas' version of Los Santos also tries to capture the surrounding area that would one day becoe Blaine County, but hardware limitations would prevent Rockstar from bringing it to life anything like as clearly as it did in GTA 5.

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews.

According to recent reports, GTA 6's take, however, could be one of its most fascinating features. Miami, while iconic, isn't quite as ubiquitous as NY or LA, but Florida as a whole as certainly carved out an identity within popular culture. Rockstar's ability to build out the rest of Leonida is likely what will give vast swathes of GTA 6 the kind of identity that Garbutt was discussing when it came to GTA 5. And with the depth of Red Dead Redemption 2 and the last 13 years of hardware advancements behind it, expectations will be extremely high. It's felt like there's a real desire to expand on the roleplaying aspect of GTA 6, and bringing the entirety of Vice City and its surroundings to life will be a massive part of that.

As we get ready to wrap up the working week here at Pure Xbox, we wanted to alert you to a couple of new updates that have been pushed out in recent days - one for Xbox consoles in general, and another specifically for GTA 6.

The Xbox console revision was actually released on Wednesday, but nobody made a song and dance about it whatsoever, while the patch notes only referenced "general stability and performance improvements".

However, we now know that the upgrade was related to the addition of achievements in four original Xbox games, and unless you download the update, you won't be able to see those achievements right now.

There's a chance your console may have downloaded this automatically but to check, go to "Settings", "System", "Updates" and then see if there's an upgrade waiting to be downloaded or not.

Here's a video version of how to do it:.

It has been revealed that as for GTA 6, in addition to the 200GB+ preload that went live a few days ago, there's also now a fresh enhancement as of a few hours ago that sits at around 2.2GB. You'll need to download this in order to start playing on November 19th.

Sources indicate that some people are speculating that this might be the so-called "day one patch", but who knows whether we might get another one between now and next Thursday. In any case, you'll want to get this queued up as soon as possible (unless you haven't installed the game yet, in which case it'll be included in your initial download).

Sources indicate that there's a chance you may see a different size, but it's somewhere around that 2.2GB mark. We're also spotting that some people haven't got it yet for whatever reason, but it should roll out to all Xbox consumers in the very near future.

Don't forget that Alpha Skip-Ahead Xbox Insiders have also received a special latest update this week that adds three new features for testing purposes, so if you're part of the Insider programme, keep an eye out for that.

We'll be back next week with loads more coverage on the GTA 6 launch, and here's hoping there are no more downloads to get us ready for November 19th. Just a few more sleeps until the big day!

#17032. Substantial Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Substantial Walk developer House House reveal genAI use in final stretch of development, only revealing it now as "it has become a matter of public interest"

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Friendslop du jour Substantial Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!).
  • It has been revealed that A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset.
  • According to recent reports, so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Friendslop du jour Substantial Walk is the latest in an unfortunately long series of games that have been confirmed to use generative AI in their production, with developers House House clarifying their use of it in a statement to Aftermath (thanks!). House House state that "LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs", and that "well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage", but are quick to note that "generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.".

It has been revealed that A specific example is given in the case of Unity's apparent weirdness around shadow casters in its rendering pipeline, as it's seemingly difficult to have unnecessary shadow casters behind the player culled, which resulted in the game running at half speed around sunrise and sunset. House House explain that they couldn't find a solution themselves, asked a Unity engineer for help who mentioned it was impossible, and then decided the only answer was to ask an LLM chatbot; "after a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code." While absolutely not the most pressing thing to mention here, it is very funny to me for House House to clarify that they "had to modify the suggestion extensively", almost as if this tech isn't actually helpful in giving useful answers.

According to recent reports, so, House House touched the stove, despite how easy it is to simply not touch the stove. The thing is, this wasn't a case of being forced to by upper management, as is sometimes the case. This was a choice made entirely voluntarily, and House House are attempting to have their cake and eat it by ending their statement with the reflection that "We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Massive Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards." But then, you know, that's followed up by saying that Big Walk was developed "without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards." So, not to worry, they learned touching the stove is bad by touching the stove, and definitely won't do it again in future. If only there were thousands of other cases informing them why touching the stove is bad.

Very relevant to this reveal is the recent statement by select jurors of the Independent Games Festival which, after much internal deliberation, came to the conclusion that those who sign the statement would decline to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity, with signees including Austin Walker, Sam Barlow, Lena Reine, Brendon Chung, Aura Triolo, aurahack and more. The statement specifies that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms." Fellow juror Liz Ryerson confirmed that Major Walk was being considered by the IGF, and was a matter of discussion in judging as to whether its use of genAI would be acceptable.

As for House House only disclosing this now, they state it was not only because it was necessary for their IGF submission, but also that "we have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage", and that they have spoken on it publicly to Aftermath because "it has become a matter of public interest.".

In a recent development, if I were to be cynical, I would say that House House would prefer to be the ones breaking this news themselves rather than having the IGF reveal that they had been hiding their use up until now; it's usually easier to control PR if you release it yourself. Massive Walk had already been securely in everyone's good books for its support for the BDS boycott, for example, so why ruin that clean rep with something like a genAI disclosure?

I don't know how better to close this article than with an excerpt from that very IGF statement:.

"We know that change does not come at the individual level, but as independent developers, we also know firsthand the value of pushing back on what an industry has deemed "inevitable." As jurists, we feel a responsibility to push past defeatism and aspire to a higher ideal.

The future is not yet settled. You are not alone. We can stand together.".

Recent findings suggest that one of the biggest reveals out of today’s Xbox Partner Preview showcase has been the upcoming Stalker 2 expansion. The developer did tease some sort of announcement ahead of the event, but I don’t think an expansion was on many of our bingo cards.

Sources indicate that cost of Hope is the major news; a new add-on that the developer has wisely decided to reveal fairly close to release. Or, at least, the planned release target.

First off, Cost of Hope is set for release this summer. It’ll arrive on all current platforms simultaneously, meaning PC, Xbox, and PlayStation. The expansion is described as “non-linear”, and it takes place in the heartlands, deeper into the Zone.

Sources indicate that the story revolves around a conflict between Duty, and Freedom, two factions whose idea of the what the Zone is and their understanding of its possibilities differ widely. You’ll be playing as protagonist Skif once again, and the expansion’s events will run parallel to the main game.

GSC Game World says Cost of Hope will introduce two fresh regions, offering dozens of hours of gameplay. We’ll get to actually explore the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant as part of the expansion, alongside the Iron Forest.

Each of the two latest regions will have its own hub area, NPCs, quests, activities and stories. Of course, it wouldn’t be a Stalker expansion without some new weapons, and Cost of Hope promises a few - some can even be seen in the trailer.

In a recent development, the developer also confirmed that there’s one other story DLC in the works. Together with Heart of Chornobyl, and Cost of Hope all three will form a trilogy of interconnected stories. More details on Cost of Hope - including a release date - will be revealed sometime in the summer.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A teenager who went missing in Utah more than 17 months ago has been rescued from a home in Oregon after she got in touch with another young player in Among Us.

According to a federal criminal complaint reported by Newsweek and KUTV (via IGN), the girl, who was 15 when she disappeared from Garden City, Utah, on 29th May 2025, began chatting with another teenager in Among Us on or around 15th October this year.

Recent findings suggest that the pair later moved their conversation to a different social media app, where she told them who she was and that she was being held against her will in Oregon. She had been given a phone with no cellular data, which meant she could only get online via wi-fi.

Recent findings suggest that the other teen told their parent, who contacted the FBI on 1st November. Agents listened in on a video call between the parent and the girl, and she was recovered from the house later that day. She is now 17.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, of Huntington, Oregon, was arrested during a traffic stop.

According to recent reports, according to the US Attorney's Office for the District of Utah, he allegedly met the girl online in May 2025, then drove to Utah to pick her up and took her back to his home across state lines. He was charged on 2nd November with transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity, and made his first court appearance in Boise, Idaho, on 4th November.

Sources indicate that "Our priority in this case was the safe return of the minor victim," said US Attorney Melissa Holyoak. "Those who allegedly exploit and prey upon the most vulnerable members of our communities will be relentlessly investigated and held accountable.".

Utah's US Attorney's Office stresses that a complaint is merely an allegation, and that all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty in a court of law.
